newsitem.title: USA: Storms cut power, cause flash floods in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: Storms cut power, cause flash floods in Kansas.

text.p: Strong thunderstorms pounded central and southeast Kansas Friday morning, cutting power to thousands of residents and stranding dozens of motorists in flash floods.

Wichita firefighters rescued a pregnant woman who began experiencing labour pains as her car was trapped in three feet of water. Deputy Fire Chief Michael Rudd said a pumper truck transported the woman to a Wichita hospital, where she gave birth.

"I've been with the Wichita Fire Department for 27 years and I've never seen this much of the city flooded this severely," Rudd said. "We had all sorts of problems -- vehicle accidents, basement walls caving in, downed power lines."
KGE, a unit of Western Resources Inc, said approximately 20,000 customers lost power service Friday morning after wind gusts as high as 60 miles per hour downed trees and power lines.
KGE said 8,000 customers in Wichita remained without power as of 10:30 a.m. EDT, and about 300 workers were trying to restore service.
"It was really rocking and rolling last night," said Suzanne Coin, a KGE spokeswoman. "The storm came through and just sat here for a while."
